summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted with hypoxia and pneumonia that failed outpatient levofloxacin treatment. She had a history of recurrent pneumonias and T2 paraplegia. In the ED, she presented with fever, low oxygen saturation, and hypotension, requiring a right internal jugular central line and IV fluids. She was started on vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam for healthcare-associated pneumonia. Monitoring in the MICU showed stable blood pressure, and she was transferred to the floor. Urine culture grew ESBL-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae, likely colonizing due to chronic catheter use, but covered by antibiotics. Sputum and blood cultures showed no concerning pathogens. She improved clinically, was transitioned to oral Augmentin, and discharged home on room air after the central line was removed. Chronic conditions including hypothyroidism, anxiety, depression, and anemia were managed throughout.
